contradictions: CAM Unified already has a v1 contract, and no reader saw it. superlearner_reuse says neither lineage is a CAM Unified prototype and calls CAM_UNIFIED_SPEC.md 'untracked'. llm_integration says there is no Unified OpenWorld adapter and calls superlearner/unified/interfaces.py the 'CAM Unified' ObservationBatch slot. In fact commit 2387fa1 (HEAD~1 on feat/cam-7.0-unified) tracks the spec and adds /workspace/agentrs/superlearner/src/superlearner/cam_unified/interfaces.py (CONTRACT_VERSION=1: Observation, ToolSchema, Action, ExecutionResult, EventRecord, DecisionTrace, GoalSpec, IndependentGoalResult, EnvAdapter, GoalEvaluator, TokenSet, OutcomeBatch, FastState, EntityRegistry, ArchiveP, CheckpointOpsP ...), plus config.py (SCALES dev 8x384x6/32 ... large), testing.py (doubles), CAM_UNIFIED_ARCHITECTURE.md, CAM_UNIFIED_LEDGER.md and CAM_UNIFIED_COMPLETION.json. All 71 completion requirements are NOT_STARTED, including A12 archive, A16 distributed, A17 OpenWorld adapter and F01 durable queue. superlearner/unified is CAM 6.1 (its __init__ docstring says so). Two different classes are both named ObservationBatch: unified.interfaces.ObservationBatch is tensors (values, deltas, present, ids, text, text_mask); cam_unified.interfaces.ObservationBatch is records (env_ids, observations, t, done).

The v1 contract contradicts the real Crucible semantics in four places. (a) Observation.t and ToolSchema.duration_hint are float days, and EnvAdapter.collect_events(since: Sequence[float]) is time-based. Crucible time is integer seconds from 0 at genesis, the cursor is the event seq, and many events share one t (all genesis events at t=0; rig.report and bank.txn at the same tick second), so a time cursor is ambiguous. (b) ExecutionResult.duration means 'simulated days consumed', but World.execute never moves the clock. (c) testing.py examples use 'USD/month', while Crucible money is integer cents everywhere. (d) config max_arg_tokens=384 and sem_chunk_tokens=256, but measured Qwen3 tokens are 1,068 for the competent control's code.commit args and about 11.7k for each use.examples result.

Reward sparsity. ow_agent_api says RewardContract is 0 on most steps and changes only at daily checks. I drove ExampleInductor only through WorldServer actor calls. Step reward was nonzero on 47 of 144 hourly steps on ow_tiny seed 1 and 18 of 96 on ow_market seed 1, summing to 2.0 (progress 1 plus success bonus 1). The shaping is shaping*dPhi over a windowed revenue metric, recomputed at every step_reward. It is identically 0 only for agents that never earn, which so far is every learned and LLM agent.

SessionCore is not an OpenWorld 4.0 protocol, although superlearner_reuse calls it 'the trusted OpenWorld session protocol'. superlearner/world/tasks.py has TRAIN_FAMILIES=('tiny','bazaar','cheap_compute_closed_markets','expensive_compute_open_distribution'), and no superlearner source references any ow_* family. Its Evaluator also calls GoalVerifier.daily_check every 6 simulated hours (next_check += 6*3600). RewardContract checks every DAY (check_every_s=DAY) and run_open_economy checks at the end of each day, so a 'sustained for k daily checks' goal means something different in SessionCore.

Readers give different clocks as 'the' OpenWorld clock. Runner advances a fixed dt (default 600; experiments use 3600). CrucibleEnv uses dt=60 with time_mode fixed/cost/none. WorldEnv advances cost_s + think_s(600). SessionCore advances cost_s (at least 1 s) per execute, plus think_s=60, plus wait (at most 3 days). run_mechanism uses dt=1800 and CrucibleAdapter dt=3600. ow_goals_worldgen calls cost-based time 'realistic' while ow_agent_api calls cost_s 'bookkeeping'. At kernel level only advance_time moves the clock, so action duration is purely a harness choice that the contract must fix.

Lever spec field names differ. research_mech reports Lever(name, lo, hi, default, integer). The in-world rig.spec tool returns levers as {name, min, max, default, integer, doc} (measured on ow_works; my probe crashed on KeyError 'lo'). A MechWorldAdapter and an OpenWorldAdapter built from the two readers would encode the same facility differently.

MechVecEnv horizons. superlearner_reuse says episodes are 96-120 ticks. research_mech lists 96-192 (scm_delay 144, abm_wom 160, scm_regime 192). Both are below T_MAX=256, so 'the cap never fired' still holds. An OpenWorld lifetime at 24 decisions per day passes 256 decisions on day 11.

'tiny' and 'ow_tiny' are different families. ow_goals_worldgen's 'tiny: 141 tools, 0.31 s/day, ~960 events/day' is the classic 3.0 family. ow_agent_api's 'ow_tiny: 145 tools, 0.12 s/day, ~1,063 events/day' is OpenWorld 4.0. The SL4 / SessionCore results are on the classic family, not OpenWorld.

GPU. llm_integration reports a '12 GB cap' and says 'the GPU is shared'; superlearner_reuse says one 49 GB A6000. nvidia-smi now shows the RTX A6000 at 1 MiB used of 49,140 MiB and 0% utilisation. The 12 GB was the readers' own brief limit, not a hardware constraint.

answered_gaps.question: What does an actor actually receive in OpenWorld? (Needed for observation and event-token design.)
answered_gaps.answer: Measured by driving ExampleInductor only through WorldServer.observe/available_tools/execute_action (script /tmp/claude-0/-workspace/8a8c4e56-2384-4271-b874-3a6441f3bc23/scratchpad/understand/critic/p1_events.py). Volume: ow_tiny s1 had 364 actor-visible events in 6 days (about 60 per day), against about 1,000 events per day in the world. ow_market s1 had 447 in 4 days (about 110 per day). Types and payload keys: bank.txn [by,id,kind,memo,postings,ref] (dominant); forum.post [author,board,body,hosts,id,tags,title]; market.rating [buyer,id,listing,seller,stars,text]; market.listing; market.listing_update [changes,id]; know [id,kind,principal,value] (tool-discovery signal); id.person; id.org; id.member; biz.registered; bank.account; code.repo; code.commit; cloud.instance; cloud.deployment (includes the manifest); code.compute [day,ms,principal]; use.probe [... mean, failures, fee]. ow_market adds ops.request and cloud.provider_price. Payload size is 22-236 Qwen tokens (bank.txn about 79, forum.post about 102, cloud.deployment 236). Observation.summary is tiny, about 210 chars: identity.orgs {o:..: role}, bank.balances {acct_id: cents}, mail.unread, cloud.services {host: 'ok'}, and in ow_market ops.open_requests. Everything else numeric arrives in tool results (for example use.report has 23 numeric fields) or in events.

answered_gaps.question: Units and timestamps the adapter must convert.
answered_gaps.answer: Time: Event.t and Observation.time are integer simulated seconds. create_world leaves now=0 (measured), and an actor joins at t=0 unless the goal has warmup_s. The world.clock tool returns {time, day: t//86400, hour}. annotations.costSeconds is in seconds and never moves the clock. Money is integer cents. bank.txn postings are [[account, +/-cents], ...]. Field names are inconsistent: *_cents (price_cents, fee_cents, charged_cents, revenue_cents, cost_cents, price_core_hour_cents), but also bank.transfer.amount (documented only as 'cents'), cloud.provider/instance 'price' (cents per core-hour), market.listing 'price' (cents per call) and use.probe 'fee'. rig.spec states money.unit 'cents' explicitly. Time-valued arguments mix units: *_s, days, hours, in_s, period_s. The contract's float days and 'USD' need an explicit conversion table in the adapter.

answered_gaps.question: What entity identifiers exist, and how do I extract them for EntityRegistry?
answered_gaps.answer: There is no uniform scheme. Prefixed forms: principals 'p:<handle>', orgs 'o:<handle>', service principals 'svc:<host>'. Numbered forms: accounts 'acct_000017', transactions 'tx_', listings 'lst_', instances 'inst_', deployments 'dep_', docs 'doc_', posts 'fpost_', probes 'probe_'. Repos are '<org>/<name>' and commits are hex. Hosts are bare strings ('nova-decode', 'trans0svc1'). Categories look like 'gen.transform.c704a121'. Composite ids: ratings 'lst_000001|p:customer-09|0', knowledge 'p:nova|host|x'. The rig is 'works' with seat ints and neutral lever/gauge names ('ji31', 'pe11'). A regex over payload strings finds only p:/o:/svc:. Extraction must therefore be key-driven: id, owner, seller, buyer, author, holder, founder, org, person, principal, account, provider, instance, host, repo, listing, commit, rig, seat, category/need, plus posting pairs.

answered_gaps.question: Is causal provenance (Observation.caused_by, EventRecord.attributed_to) available from Crucible?
answered_gaps.answer: Partly, and the native API discards it. Event.cmd (core/kernel.py) is the global command number of the transaction that emitted the event; scheduled-process events have cmd=None and actor 'sys'. WorldServer's compact_event() (api/local.py:208) keeps only {seq,t,type,actor,payload}, dropping cmd and vis. ActionResult.to_dict() drops ActionResult.events (the seqs the command emitted). replay_events keeps cmd (41 cmd-tagged events in my ow_tiny run). Direct consequences can be linked if the trusted adapter reads w.events_range(cursor) filtered by w.visible(e, w.principals_of(p)) and maps cmd to its own action_id. Delayed consequences carry no pointer. They must be attributed from domain payloads: rig.report carries the tick 't' and the 'settings' in force, matching rig.set's applies_at_tick; bank.txn carries kind/memo/ref. Customer purchases and ratings have no link to the action that caused them. Because cmd is a global counter, strip it from other actors' events. The actor's own successful commands' events (rig.set, code.repo, know, ...) do appear in observe (only 'cmd' and 'cmd.rejected' are hidden); mark them evidence=CONTROLLED.

answered_gaps.question: Can a cursor-based observe lose events, and what is in the first observation?
answered_gaps.answer: Yes, events can be lost. WorldServer.observe keeps the newest max_events (default 50, constructor arg) and drops the rest, reporting the count in `dropped`. It still advances the cursor to w.seq, so the dropped events are gone for that actor. It also scans back at most max_scan=200,000 events. Use WorldServer(max_events=100_000) or the operator log; observe still cost 0.5-0.65 ms mean (2.2 ms max). The cursor starts just before join (join_world sets _Session(cursor=seq0)). The first observation therefore contains the join events (bank.account, the endowment bank.txn) but none of the genesis public events: need-format docs (docs.create bodies of 81-202 tokens), listings, providers, persons, forum boards (169 seqs in ow_tiny, 399 in ow_market). Those arrive only through tools (search/docs/market.browse) or replay_events(wid, 0, None, actor=ident), which took 0.08 s for 433 events on ow_tiny and 0.18 s for 562 on ow_market. collect_events should use a per-environment seq cursor, not a time float.

answered_gaps.question: Can the goal evaluator run against a WorldServer-managed world, and how should advance_time interact with it?
answered_gaps.answer: Yes. Recipe: wid = srv.create_world({'family': g.world['family'], 'overrides': g.world['overrides']}, g.world['seed']); ident = srv.join_world(wid, handle, endowment=g.endowment); then GoalVerifier(g, ident.principal).begin(srv.world(wid)), or RewardContract(g).begin(w, principal). For warmup_s, call srv.advance_time(wid, dt=warmup_s), which matches instantiate()'s idle Runner. Measured: ExampleInductor reached verified success on day 4 on ow_tiny s1 (same as the reader's Runner result) and on day 3 on ow_market s1, a new result. Two caveats. First, RewardContract.step_reward handles a clock jump of more than a day by running every due daily_check against the end state (the while loop at goals/contracts.py:220). EnvAdapter.advance_time(duration) must therefore split waits at day boundaries and call the evaluator at each one, or sustain streaks are miscounted. Second, bindings() credits only orgs where the actor's role is 'owner'. Map IndependentGoalResult from GoalVerifier.status(): success -> achieved, progress -> score, streak, success_t and initially_true -> details.

answered_gaps.question: Is there a dense, numeric, typed-argument task inside the real OpenWorld, usable for a 2-day vertical path without generating code?
answered_gaps.answer: Yes: the ow_works facility (script p3_rig.py in the critic scratch directory). Tools: rig.list -> [{rig:'works', tick_s:3600, lease_cents:20000, seats:[...]}]; rig.spec(rig) -> {levers:[{name,min,max,default,integer,doc}], gauges:[{name}], brief (natural-language objective), horizon_ticks:96, money:{unit:'cents',...}}; rig.take(rig, seat=0); rig.set(rig, settings={lever: float}) -> {settings, clipped, applies_at_tick, applies_at}; rig.read(rig) -> {report:{readings{gauge: float}, revenue_cents, cost_cents, net_cents, shortfall_cents, score, settings}}; plus rig.release, rig.history and rig.hypothesize. Each tick sends an asynchronous rig.report event (actor 'sys') and a bank.txn. One set plus read costs 0.28 ms and one simulated hour 6.9 ms. Evaluator metrics: rig_net and rig_score, both (principal, rig, window_s=0), and rig_ticks(rig) (mechanisms/module.py:739-751). Random settings lose money (net -3,612 cents on tick 0), so there is a real learning signal. ow_works has no validated normalisation (default/oracle net); compute it on the evaluator side from the spec's mechanism config if a score in [0,1] is needed.

answered_gaps.question: What do tool schemas look like, for typed argument heads and a constrained decoder?
answered_gaps.answer: Script p2_tools.py. ow_tiny: 145 tools, 20 hosts, 64 read-only; on average 2.4 args per tool (max 10); 12 take no args. Leaf types: 242 string, 59 integer, 29 string-enum, 1 integer-enum, 8 boolean, 3 number, 9 array; 15 patterns. Free-form objects: code.commit.files (path -> string up to 65,536 chars), contracts.propose.clauses[], contracts.sign.accounts, goals.propose.predicate, world.validate.args; code.run.input is untyped. ow_works adds rig.set.settings and rig.hypothesize. ow_market: 200 tools, 27 hosts, 27 free-form objects (caps, deal, gov, db, wf, net.fetch.form). Schema keywords are limited to the subset in core/schema.py: type (possibly a list), properties, required, additionalProperties (default False), enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, items, minItems, maxItems, default, description. check_schema admits agent-deployed schemas, which can be {'type':'object','additionalProperties':true}. costSeconds ranges 0-600 s. Catalogue size: 82k JSON chars and 16.2k Qwen3 tokens for ow_tiny (mean 110, max 496 per tool). The validator is crucible.core.schema.validate(schema, value) -> list[str]; World.execute applies with_defaults and then validates.

answered_gaps.question: How large are real arguments and observations in Qwen3 tokens?
answered_gaps.answer: Script p4_tokens.py, Qwen3-1.7B tokenizer on CPU, ExampleInductor on ow_tiny. Argument tokens: code.commit 1,068 (service.py plus crucible.json), code.run 922 (the input example), market.list 103, bank.transfer 46, every other call under 40. Result tokens: use.examples 11,727 and 11,834, code.run 641, use.categories 513, use.report 219-333, most others under 110. An agent that sells a working service must emit about 1k-token code arguments. At the measured eager decode of 31 ms per step that is about 33 s per code action (about 13 s with compiled static cache).

answered_gaps.question: How does the rate limit work?
answered_gaps.answer: Per principal, per simulated clock hour (hour = now // 3600), set by spec.params max_actions_per_hour=240 in ow_* families. _ap_cmd increments the counter only on accepted 'cmd' events; rejected calls emit cmd.rejected and do not count. The 241st accepted call in the same hour returns error code 'rate_limited'. Since execution never moves time, an adapter that allows many calls per decision without advance_time will hit this.

answered_gaps.question: What does a world cost in RAM and disk over a lifetime?
answered_gaps.answer: Script p5_mem.py: ow_market, 15 simulated days, one call per hour, 38,430 events. RSS grew 66 MB with memory:// (about 4.4 MB per simulated day; events live both in World.log and in MemoryStore) and 38 MB with sqlite://, whose file was 12 MB (about 0.8 MB per day). Wall time was 0.45 s per simulated day. World.log_retain defaults to 2,000,000 events. Beyond that, a world without a store raises ProtocolError on events_range for trimmed seqs. A 90-day world is about 0.4 GB of RAM, so 16 worlds are about 6 GB.

answered_gaps.question: What durable-storage and transport building blocks are actually available?
answered_gaps.answer: pyarrow 26.0.1 and sqlite 3.54.1 are in the venv. 250 GB of overlay disk is free; RAM is 125 GB total with about 82 GB available; 48 CPUs; the process runs as root; /var/tmp/crucible-sbx is mode 711, which the sandbox needs. Existing transports are all in-memory. crucible.scale.rollout.RolloutFarm uses private pipes plus a bounded queue, a hash-based param_version and backpressure, and is not durable. superlearner RolloutPool is synchronous. agentrs selfplay InferenceEngine/Collector keeps an fsync'd JSONL sink but discards an episode when the version changes. Cam7Learner replay is a pickled .replay.npy. Nothing has a spool with dedup, segment rename or recovery, so F01 and A12 are greenfield. The ledger records that the Vast rental ends 2026-11-30 03:00 UTC with no persistent volume, and that git push needs the user's go-ahead.

answered_gaps.question: Is hidden state reachable from the agent side, and does the economy reward garbage?
answered_gaps.answer: World.state, World.spec, query and system_call are plain attributes and methods, so isolation is by API discipline only. Leaks: GET /v1/worlds/{w} (api/http_server.py:304) authenticates an actor token and returns world_info with family and seed. Observation.world_id is 'w-'+spec.hash()[:12]. The adapter must not pass either to the model. Sandboxed agent code cannot read the repo (Landlock returns EACCES). Garbage does not earn: docs/OPENWORLD_REPORT.md:249 says 'garbage service earned nothing despite a better listing and price'. Revenue therefore requires a correct decoder program (ExampleInductor runs induce_wire_formats and then wire_solver_source), so a learned agent's economy reward stays 0 until it writes working code.

unanswered: My input was truncated. The sixth reader's map (actors/self-play, per CAM_UNIFIED_LEDGER.md) was missing, and superlearner_reuse stops mid-interface at export_weights. I could not cross-check them.

Architect decision, not answerable from code: the single clock policy for the adapter. Options are fixed dt per decision, cost_s-based SMDP, or event-driven waits. Also needed: how many actions per simulated hour and per decision (rate limit 240/h), and what ExecutionResult.duration means when execution consumes no simulated time.

Architect decision: whether TOOL tokens (145 in ow_tiny, 200 in ow_market, growing as hosts are discovered) sit inside F_theta's max_ctx_tokens=384 context or only in the ActionGenerator's pointer set. If inside, tools take 38-52% of the per-step budget before O, B(17), M(<=64) and G(<=8).

Architect decision: whether Qwen LoRA trains during Stage 1. The contract keys the hidden-state cache by (sha256, version) and never serves it across versions, so every semantic update forces re-encoding all replayed observations and tool schemas (16k tokens of catalogue per world, ~12k per use.examples result). No budget for this exists.

Not measured, because I did not load models on the GPU: end-to-end wall time and memory of the contract's dev/main core plus Qwen3-1.7B. That covers encode, act with pointer and typed heads, Qwen argument decoding, and the log_prob recompute and backward. Also not measured: the GPU memory of N actor processes, each holding a Qwen copy as spec 14.1 implies ('versioned copy of shared model parameters').

No validated normalisation exists for the mechanism inside ow_works, and no GoalContract family uses rig_net. The success threshold, horizon and default/oracle baselines for an OpenWorld rig task must be defined and validated (TaskValidator needs explicit controls).

No non-privileged control exists for specified or experiential categories, and no learned positive control exists in any ow_* economy. It is therefore unknown which first OpenWorld economy task a learned agent can solve at all: ExampleInductor is scripted program induction and Builder uses hidden reference solvers.

Open question for the archive design: should EventRecord.observations store the actor view only (as the contract says), and how should genesis public events be stored, given they are visible but absent from observe? Also: is the archive a separate store from Crucible's own hash-chained event log (sqlite store), or does it reference that log's seqs?
Multi-agent semantics (OW-7, W05) are undecided: several CAM actors sharing one world and one operator clock, versus independent worlds per actor. EnvAdapter's batch [B] does not say which.
risks: 1. Generating valid executable actions with an untrained, latent-conditioned decoder. Evidence: CAM2 with prefix-conditioned Qwen3-0.6B on Crucible had 70% schema rejections and 0 successes; frozen 1.7B mostly fails the schema; frozen 4B loops on one call. No grammar or jsonschema library is installed. The competent control's code.commit is 1,068 tokens against max_arg_tokens=384. Eager decode is 31 ms per token, about 33 s per code action; the 2.6x faster compiled path diverges in tokens and logprobs from the training forward. Mitigation for the 2-day path: a hand-written LogitsProcessor that forces '{"tool": "' and a tool-name trie (mask width 151,936); typed heads for numbers, enums and booleans; pointer heads for ids seen in observations; validation with crucible.core.schema.validate; behaviour logprobs recomputed via the learner path. Choose Stage-1 actions that need no free-text code: ow_works rig.take/set/read plus read-only discovery tools.

2. No learning signal in the real OpenWorld economy for a learned agent. Every learned and LLM agent so far earns exactly 0 independent revenue; the garbage service earns nothing; revenue requires a correct program. RewardContract is then 0 on every step, so a PPO update would be vacuous noise, and the 'weight update' requirement would be met only formally. Mitigation: make Stage 1's update driven by dense, verifiable targets the adapter can expose: per-action ok/error.code (13 codes with structured details), bank balance deltas in cents, rig.report revenue_cents/cost_cents/readings each simulated hour, use.report fields. Use ow_works rig_net as the first RL return, and keep the economy goal as evaluation only.

3. Adapter semantics bugs that silently lose data or leak hidden state. WorldServer.observe drops events beyond max_events=50 while advancing the cursor. compact_event strips cmd (provenance) and ActionResult.to_dict strips the emitted event seqs. Genesis public events never appear in observe. Time is integer seconds with seq cursors, while the contract uses float days and time-based since. RewardContract runs all daily checks against the end state after a multi-day jump; SessionCore checks every 6 h. There is a 240/h accepted-action limit. Hidden state is guarded only by in-process discipline (World.state is reachable; /v1 world_info leaks family and seed). Mitigation: a trusted operator-side adapter that reads w.events_range with w.visible() and the seq cursor, keeps cmd mapped to own action ids, chunks advance_time at day boundaries and calls GoalVerifier at each, converts cents and seconds explicitly, and is guarded by a test that the learner process receives only these records.

4. Compute and memory on one A6000 with Qwen in the loop. Semantic encoding with LoRA invalidates the version-keyed cache on every update: the tool catalogue is 16.2k tokens per ow_tiny world, use.examples ~11.7k per result, prefill ~18k tok/s, so a single re-encode of one tool catalogue costs ~1 s. Backward through 1.7B needs gradient checkpointing (8x520 tokens at 4.4 GB, otherwise more than 12 GB). Per-actor model copies on one 48 GB GPU (spec 14.1) leave little room for the learner. Worlds are single-threaded Python at 5-19 ms per simulated hour each, so B in-process worlds serialise on one core. Mitigation for Stage 1: Qwen frozen as encoder with cached hidden states (LoRA only on the decoder adapter, with its own version); dev scale; one GPU process doing batched inference and learning; worlds in CPU worker processes (48 cores).

5. Durable persistence and transport are entirely greenfield under a hard deadline, while 8 workstreams code in parallel against a contract that already diverges from the code. A12/F01/A16/A17 are NOT_STARTED; existing transports (RolloutFarm pipes, Collector JSONL that discards on version change, pickled Cam7 replay) do not meet spec 14.2. Disk is ephemeral and the rental ends 2026-11-30 03:00 UTC, with git as the only authorised durable destination. Divergences: ObservationBatch name collision, days vs seconds, lo/hi vs min/max, max_arg_tokens. Mitigation: freeze contract v2 first with the unit, cursor and provenance fixes. Build the archive as append-only Parquet/JSONL segments with write-tmp, fsync and rename, plus a SQLite index (pyarrow 26 and sqlite 3.54 are present). Stamp model_version on every EventRecord from day one, so the async V-trace path can be added without re-recording.
